title: Component Communication 📡
description: Pass data into child components with @Input() and emit events upward with @Output().

slides.title: Parent‑Child Component Communication 👨‍👧
slides.content:
# Sharing Data Between Components

Angular apps are a tree of components. To build something useful, they need to talk to each other.

* **Parent → Child**: Pass data using `@Input()`.
* **Child → Parent**: Emit events using `@Output()` (EventEmitter).

This one‑way data flow makes your app predictable and easier to debug.

slides.title: @Input() – Receiving Data from Parent
slides.content: In the child component, decorate a property with `@Input()` to turn it into a bindable input.

quizData.question: Which decorator allows a child component to receive data from a parent?
quizData.explanation: `@Input()` marks a property as a data‑binding target for parent components.

slides.title: @Output() – Emitting Events Upward 📤
slides.content:
When the child needs to tell the parent something happened (e.g., a button click), it uses `@Output()` and an `EventEmitter`.

* Decorate an `EventEmitter` instance with `@Output()`.
* Call `.emit(value)` to send data to the parent.
* In the parent template, use event binding: `(customEvent)="handleEvent($event)"`.

slides.title: Naming Convention for Outputs 🏷️
slides.content: Name the output property after the event, e.g., `(itemSelected)`, `(formSubmitted)`. Avoid prefixing with `on` – the binding already looks event‑ish.

slides.title: Template Reference Variables 📍
slides.content:
Sometimes you need to access a child component’s method or property directly from the parent template (without using @Output). You can use a **template reference variable** with `#child`.

```html
<app-child #childRef></app-child>
<button (click)="childRef.someMethod()">Call Child</button>
```

Use with caution – it couples the parent to the child’s public API. `@Input`/`@Output` is usually cleaner.

quizData.question: An @Output() property must be of type EventEmitter.
quizData.explanation: Angular uses EventEmitter (which extends RxJS Subject) to emit custom events. It’s the standard type for outputs.

slides.title: Recap: The Component Data Flow 🌊
slides.content:
## Summary of Bindings

| Direction | Syntax |
|-----------|--------|
| Component → Template (one‑way) | `{{ expression }}` or `[property]="value"` |
| Template → Component (one‑way) | `(event)="handler()"` |
| Two‑way (both) | `[(ngModel)]="property"` |
| Parent → Child | `[inputProp]="data"` with `@Input()` |
| Child → Parent | `(outputProp)="handler($event)"` with `@Output()` |

Now you’re equipped to build dynamic, interactive Angular interfaces!
